price.aPreRelease: During the pre-release period, every feature is available free of charge. When billing starts, you will be notified at least 30 days in advance and can choose between the Basic, Intermediate and Pro plans.
price.aEnforced: Every new account starts with 30 free days of the Pro plan, with no card required. After that, you choose between the Basic, Intermediate and Pro plans, billed monthly or yearly, and can cancel at any time.

offline.q: Do I need internet during the show?
offline.a: No. Installed as an app, Setlyst keeps your repertoire on the device and Live Mode works without a connection. Changes made offline are sent when the network returns.

bands.q: Can I use it with my band?
bands.a: Yes. Create a band, invite the members by link and set each one's role. The band's repertoire, setlists, gigs and tours are available to everyone, according to their permissions.

content.q: Does Setlyst provide lyrics and chords?
content.a: No. You add your own repertoire, by typing or importing ChordPro files. Other artists' lyrics and chords are protected by copyright; keeping them for rehearsal and performance is the responsibility of whoever adds them.

devices.q: Which devices does it work on?
devices.a: Any current browser on a phone, tablet or computer. You can also install Setlyst as an app from the browser on Android, iOS, Windows, macOS and Linux.

data.a: Your data is used only to provide the service, in line with Brazil's LGPD. You can export all your content at any time and delete your account in the settings. Details in the Privacy Policy.

free.q: Do I have to pay to use it now?
free.aPreRelease: No. During the pre-release period, every feature is available free of charge. We will give at least 30 days' notice by e-mail and in the platform before billing starts, and no plan is ever taken out or charged without your express confirmation.
free.aEnforced: Every new account gets 30 free days of the Pro plan, with no card required. After that, you choose a plan to keep the paid features.

trialEnd.q: What happens when the trial ends?
trialEnd.a: If you have not subscribed to a plan, nothing is charged: your content stays saved and your features become those of an account without a plan. If you subscribed during the trial, the first charge happens on the date shown when you subscribed, and we let you know by e-mail 7 days before.

cancel.q: Can I cancel at any time?
cancel.a: Yes, in your account settings, with no fee. The plan stays active until the end of the period already paid and is not renewed. Details in the <subscription>Subscription Terms</subscription>.

withdrawal.q: How does the right of withdrawal work?
withdrawal.a: Under article 49 of the Brazilian Consumer Protection Code, you can withdraw within 7 days of subscribing (or of the first charge, if you subscribed during the trial), with the button in Settings › Subscription or by e-mail, and get a full refund of what you paid, even if you have already used the plan. Details in the <subscription>Subscription Terms</subscription>.

limits.q: What if I go over my plan's limits?
limits.a: Nothing is deleted. You keep access to everything, but you cannot create new items of that type until you are within the limit or move to a larger plan.

credits.q: What are credits and promo codes?
credits.a: Credits can be exchanged for plan days, and promo codes grant days, credits or discounts. None of them has a cash value or can be transferred to another account.

referral.q: How does the referral programme work?
referral.a: Share your referral link. When someone creates an account and confirms their e-mail address, both accounts receive credits. There is a monthly limit of rewarded referrals; the full rules are in the <subscription>Subscription Terms</subscription>.

tonic.name: Tonic
tonic.hint: Rest: the center of the key.

tonicRelative.name: Tonic relative
tonicRelative.hint: The VIm shares two notes with the I and can stand in for it, as a tonic.

tonicAntiRelative.name: Tonic counter-relative
tonicAntiRelative.hint: The IIIm works as a tonic, less stable than the VIm; it often moves on to the VI.

relativeMajor.name: Relative major
relativeMajor.hint: The bIII is the relative tonic of the minor key.

subdominant.name: Subdominant
subdominant.hint: Moves away from the tonic and prepares the dominant.

subdominantRelative.name: Subdominant relative (cadential II)
subdominantRelative.hint: A subdominant; followed by the V it makes the II–V cadence.

subdominantMinor.name: Minor subdominant
subdominantMinor.hint: The IVm comes from the parallel minor key: a classic modal borrowing.

dominant.name: Primary dominant
dominant.hint: Tension that resolves on the tonic, a fifth below.

dominantMinorKey.name: Dominant (harmonic minor)
dominantMinorKey.hint: The V7 of the minor key, with the leading tone of the harmonic minor scale.

dominantNoRoot.name: Rootless dominant
dominantNoRoot.hint: Sounds like a V7(9) (V7(b9) in minor) without its root: a dominant.

minorFive.name: Minor V (Aeolian)
minorFive.hint: A dominant without a leading tone: a softer resolution.

subtonic.name: Subtonic (bVII)
subtonic.hint: A natural degree of the minor key; it sounds like the dominant of the {target}.

secondaryDominant.name: Secondary dominant of {target}
secondaryDominant.hint: A V7 borrowed from the {target}: it makes it a tonic for a moment and resolves on it, a fifth below.

substituteDominant.name: Substitute dominant (SubV7)
substituteDominant.hint: Shares the V7's tritone and resolves a half step down, on the tonic.

secondarySubstitute.name: Substitute dominant of {target}
secondarySubstitute.hint: The SubV7 of the {target}: the V7/{target}'s tritone, resolving a half step down onto it.

relatedTwo.name: Related II of V7/{target}
relatedTwo.hint: The cadential II of the {target}: with the V7/{target} it makes a secondary II–V leading to the {target}.

secondaryLeadingTone.name: Leading-tone diminished of {target}
secondaryLeadingTone.hint: The VII° of the {target}: its root is the leading tone rising a half step to it (a rootless V7(b9)/{target}).

diminishedAscending.name: Ascending diminished
diminishedAscending.hint: A chromatic passing chord rising a half step to the {target}; a dominant.

diminishedDescending.name: Descending diminished
diminishedDescending.hint: A chromatic passing chord falling a half step to the {target}.

diminishedAuxiliary.name: Auxiliary diminished
diminishedAuxiliary.hint: Ornaments the chord on the same root: leaves it and comes back to it.

diminished.name: Diminished chord
diminished.hint: See how it moves: passing (ascending or descending) or auxiliary.

neapolitan.name: Neapolitan chord (bII)
neapolitan.hint: A major chord on the bII, a subdominant; it usually moves to the V.

modalBorrowing.name: Modal borrowing
modalBorrowing.hint: Comes from the parallel minor key (or another mode) and colors the harmony without changing key.

augmented.name: Augmented chord
augmented.hint: A raised fifth: usually a passing chord or an altered dominant.

chromatic.name: Non-diatonic chord
chromatic.hint: Not in the key: worth a note on what it does here.

twoFive.name: II–V cadence
twoFive.hint: The II prepares the dominant, which resolves on the tonic.

twoFiveSecondary.name: Secondary II–V to {target}
twoFiveSecondary.hint: A II–V borrowed from the {target}: the II is the related II of the V7/{target}.

twoSubV.name: II–SubV7 to {target}
twoSubV.hint: The II–V cadence with the substitute dominant: the bass moves down by half steps.

extendedDominants.name: Extended dominants
extendedDominants.hint: A chain of dominants, each resolving on the next.

perfectCadence.name: Perfect cadence (V → I)
perfectCadence.hint: The dominant resolves on the tonic.

deceptiveCadence.name: Deceptive cadence
deceptiveCadence.hint: The dominant avoids the tonic and moves to the VI (or the bVI).

plagalCadence.name: Plagal cadence (IV → I)
plagalCadence.hint: The subdominant goes straight to the tonic, skipping the dominant.

backdoorCadence.name: Backdoor cadence (bVII7 → I)
backdoorCadence.hint: The dominant "through the back door": the bVII7 resolves on the tonic, a whole step up.

minorPlagalCadence.name: Minor plagal cadence (IVm → I)
minorPlagalCadence.hint: The minor subdominant, borrowed from the parallel key, resolves straight to the major tonic.

turnaround.name: Turnaround (I – VI – II – V)
turnaround.hint: The cycle that brings the harmony back to the tonic; the VI and II often become secondary dominants.

andalusian.name: Andalusian cadence (Im – bVII – bVI – V)
andalusian.hint: The bass walks down the minor tetrachord to the dominant.
